comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C13, C47, C97-C99 regarding NALCN-mediated enhancement of synaptic strength by NA. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval notes heterogeneity (2-81% range) as a caveat, while peer reviewers accept the result without raising concerns about variability.

Perfect alignment on claims C92-C93, C124 regarding cAMP independence. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to methodological limitations (no positive control, possible incomplete saturation), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, treating it as a minor mechanistic detail without questioning the experimental design.

Strong alignment on claims C14-C15, C44, C75-C80, C86-C87, C121 regarding dual GABAB receptor actions through NALCN and GIRK channels. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval provides detailed statistical validation, while peer reviewers accept it as part of comprehensive NALCN modulation demonstration.

Strong alignment on claims C70-C74, C103 regarding exclusion of GIRK channels and NALCN as primary mediator. Both evaluations support the finding. Peer reviewers note this is 'somewhat surprising' given NA's known effects on K+ channels elsewhere, while OpenEval focuses on pharmacological evidence (Ba2+ sensitivity patterns).

Strong alignment on claims C81-C85, C88 regarding NALCN expression demonstrated by low-Ca2+ test. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval emphasizes adherence to established protocols, while peer reviewers describe the electrophysiological data as 'high quality' and 'exceptional.'

Strong alignment on claims C16, C90-C91, C122, C125 regarding occlusion experiments showing shared NALCN channel populations. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval notes lack of direct structural evidence, while peer reviewers accept it as part of rigorous experimental design without raising concerns.

Alignment on claims C126-C127 regarding spatial organization of receptor pools. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval notes differential Ba2+ sensitivity as evidence but acknowledges need for direct localization studies, while peer reviewers accept the broader implications for other brain areas.

Moderate alignment on claims C10-C12, C41-C43, C100, C104 regarding NA effects mediated through NALCN inhibition. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval R2 includes additional claims (C58-C63, C68-C69) about pharmacological mechanisms that peer R2 does not explicitly address, though peer R6 covers these.

Partial alignment on claims C58-C63, C68-C69 regarding idazoxan blockade and hyperpolarization experiments. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval groups these with broader NA/NALCN mechanism claims, while peer reviewers treat them as part of experimental controls demonstrating rigor.

Moderate alignment on claims C9, C40, C51-C53 regarding loss of spontaneous firing in NALCN cKO mice. Both evaluations strongly support the finding. OpenEval R1 includes many additional claims (C8, C48-C50, C54-C57) about experimental details, while peer reviewers focus on core finding with unanimous 'unequivocal evidence' assessment.

Partial alignment on claims C64-C65 regarding preserved evoked firing in NALCN cKO. Both evaluations support the finding. OpenEval R8 includes additional claims (C66-C67) about hyperpolarization experiments, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of rigorous characterization demonstrating specificity.

Weak alignment on claims C54, C56-C57 regarding normal hearing and cell morphology in knockouts. Both evaluations support these control findings. OpenEval groups with spontaneous firing data, while peer reviewers treat as part of specificity controls within rigorous experimental design.

Both address background/contextual claims but with different focus. OpenEval R11 covers established background literature (C1-C39), while peer R12 addresses integrative conclusions and functional implications (C45-C46, C115-C117, C120, C140-C141, C146). Both are supportive but evaluate different types of claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses limitations and speculative interpretations (C105-C109, C111-C112, C133-C134, C143, C145) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate scientific caveats. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these limitation statements, though peer reviewers implicitly accept the overall rigor.
